subject.title: improve(ui): restructure Settings around user-facing pages with full agent parity

question: Should OpenClaw adopt `ui.prefs` as synchronized canonical configuration and broaden the system agent’s approval-gated configuration and plugin-management authority in this same release-sized PR?
rationale: This is a new persisted configuration contract and a deliberate change to the human-approval security boundary, so correctness tests cannot determine whether the intended long-term product and operator policy is acceptable.

options.title: Sponsor the combined direction
options.body: Approve the cross-device preference contract and widened approval-gated operations, then require focused upgrade and real-behavior evidence before merge.

options.title: Split policy from navigation
options.body: Land the settings-information architecture separately and defer `ui.prefs` plus system-agent write-policy expansion to narrower owner-reviewed PRs.

options.title: Pause the redesign
options.body: Keep the PR open but defer it until the desired settings ownership and agent-parity policy are documented by the relevant owners.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the combined direction
recommendation.body: Approve the cross-device preference contract and widened approval-gated operations, then require focused upgrade and real-behavior evidence before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The branch history supplied for this review identifies steipete as the recent contributor spanning the affected UI, configuration, and system-agent surfaces.
